For a uniformly charged sphere, the potential inside is V(r)=\frac{Q}{8\pi\varepsilon_0 R}\left(3-\frac{r^2}{R^2}\right). At the surface (r=R) this equals \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R}=16\,\text{V}. Thus \frac{Q}{8\pi\varepsilon_0 R}=8\,\text{V}. 

At point P (r=R/2): V_P=8\left(3-\frac{1}{4}\right)=8\times\frac{11}{4}=22\,\text{V}. 

At point S (r=2R, outside the sphere): V_S=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (2R)}=\frac{16}{2}=8\,\text{V}. 

Potential difference V_P-V_S=22-8=14\,\text{V}.
